**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 23:05
- [FACT] The Houston Oilers were founded in 1960 as part of the American Football League (AFL).
- [FACT] The team originally played at Jeppesen Stadium before moving to the Houston Astrodome in 1968.
- [FACT] The Houston Oilers became the first professional football team to play on artificial turf.
- [FACT] Throughout the 1970s and early 1980s, the Oilers made the playoffs 10 times and reached the AFC Championship Game twice.
- [FACT] In the late 1980s and early 1990s, the Oilers' fortunes began to decline.
- [FACT] Hall of Fame quarterback Warren Moon played for the Oilers.
- [FACT] Tension between Warren Moon and head coach Jerry Glanville led to Glanville's resignation in 1990.
- [FACT] In 1995, owner Bud Adams announced that the team would be moving to Tennessee.
- [FACT] The Oilers played their final game in Houston on December 17, 1996.
- [FACT] The team officially became the Tennessee Oilers for the 1997 season.
- [FACT] The Tennessee Oilers played in Memphis for one year before moving to Nashville and changing their name to the Tennessee Titans.
- [FACT] The Titans reached the Super Bowl in 1999 and won the AFC Championship in 2000 and 2020.
- [PREFERENCE] User expressed surprise about the Oilers being the first to play on artificial turf.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The use of artificial turf allowed for more speed and agility, as well as a more controlled and predictable bounce.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Turf was often cited as being harder on players' bodies, leading to more injuries.
- [PREFERENCE] User found it interesting that the Oilers' move to Tennessee turned out to be a good decision in the long run.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Titans have been competitive in the AFC South division, with notable players like quarterback Ryan Tannehill and running back Derrick Henry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Titans made the playoffs in 2019 and 2020 but were unable to advance past the divisional round.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Titans made key changes during the off-season to address defensive weaknesses.
- [PREFERENCE] User expressed excitement about the Titans being competitive.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Titans' first game of the 2021 NFL season is against the Arizona Cardinals on September 12, 2021.
